One-paragraph statement of the product.
Why front-ends follow the BSC Design System and why all UI lives in one lib (libs/BSC.genesis.design.system); the rules and token values themselves live in that lib's DESIGN-RULES.md.
Why every backend app (web's non-SSR backend included, and mobile's backend) standardizes on .NET 10 instead of per-team runtime choice.
Why hexagonal architecture is mandatory and kept language-agnostic across the org's projects.
Why Nx is the mandatory monorepo tool for every new project, and how boundaries/tags/generators/CI wiring keep it meaningful.
Why mobile apps standardize on React Native 0.87.x with backend-only business logic and Appium e2e, instead of a native-per-platform or client-heavy setup.
Why company web apps standardize on Next.js SSR at a pinned React/Next version instead of a client-only SPA.
Why the org holds a mandatory Gherkin-to-E2E trace and an 85% coverage floor across every project.

Why this repo mandates a test stack per project type — Vitest + Playwright for Next.js web, NUnit + Playwright for .NET backend, Jest + Appium for React Native mobile — instead of one runner picked blind for every project.
Why every app/lib in this repo defaults to TypeScript rather than plain JavaScript.
Why the runtime resolution flow escalates instead of fanning out — staged lookup costs less and keeps decisions auditable.
Why a mandated runtime version (.NET 10, react-native@0.87.x) must be checked as an installed toolchain, not just a manifest pin, before implementation starts.
Empirical map of this codebase.
Reverse-index of every guide that declares globs: in its frontmatter.
Selections captured by `keystone init`; read by the bootstrap action.

Paired ledger: [charter-debt.

TypeScript compiler (strict) — the type-check sensor's source of truth.

Every UI component comes from the design-system lib libs/BSC.genesis.design.system (@bsc/design-system), which holds all design rules, tokens and components; apps never create UI components. Read before designing or coding any UI.
Every backend app (an API/service apps/<name> — including the backend behind a non-SSR web/mobile client) is built on .NET 10, never a different runtime, and never the Next.js SSR server itself.
Hexagonal (ports & adapters) architecture, mandatory and language-agnostic, for every module in every project.
Process docs and templates are written in Spanish, matching the existing corpus.
Nx is the mandatory monorepo tool for every brand-new project, and governs any repo that already has nx.json — never a forced migration for existing non-Nx projects.
Changes under openspec/changes/ go through the openspec CLI, never hand-authored.
PowerShell scripts fail fast: $ErrorActionPreference=Stop, mandatory params, guarded Push-Location.
Mobile apps (apps/<name> shipping to iOS/Android) are built with React Native 0.87.x, keep all business logic in a dedicated backend app, and use Appium for e2e — never Playwright for native e2e.
Web apps (apps/<name> serving a browser UI) are built with Next.js SSR on React 19.2.8 / Next 16.3.4 — never a client-only SPA setup.
TDD, Gherkin-to-E2E traceability, and coverage thresholds — mandatory for every project, language-agnostic.

The mandatory unit/integration and e2e test frameworks for every project in this repo, by project type — Next.js web uses Vitest + Playwright, .NET backend uses NUnit + Playwright, React Native mobile uses Jest + Appium.
All application code in this repo is TypeScript — no new plain-JavaScript source files.
